title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Oliver Chen
description: Motivation: continuous-batcher scheduler observed occasional starvation of low-throughput/low-latency request classes and excessive queueing for short sequences under heavy throughput workloads. This PR introduces a set of scheduler tuning changes focused on queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and more predictable timeouts while preserving end-to-end throughput. Changes include: 1) introduce an "aging" priority factor so requests that wait get incremental priority boosts; 2) add a per-tenant fairness token bucket that prevents a single tenant or route from dominating batching slots; 3) implement a small preemption window for long-running batches to let latency-sensitive small requests bypass when waiting beyond a configurable threshold; 4) replace hard per-request timeouts with a smooth timeout-decay heuristic to avoid synchronized timeouts and thundering retries; 5) expose new metrics (batch_wait_seconds, request_age_percentile, preempted_batches) and add e2e bench tests and a stressbench harness; 6) configuration knobs and defaults tuned for our common production distributions. Measured improvements in internal bench runs: p99 latency for short sequences down ~20% on mixed workloads and 5-8% better sustained throughput on 8-GPU pools. The description below lists the high-level commits, changed files, review threads, and CI outcomes.

diff_snippets:
--- a/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py
+++ b/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py
@@ -120,6 +120,24 @@ def select_batch(candidates):
-    # previous first-come-first-served selection
-    chosen = fcfs(candidates)
+    # new selection: score = base_score + aging*wait_seconds - tenant_penalty
+    for c in candidates:
+        age = time.monotonic() - c.enqueue_time
+        c.score = c.base_score + config.aging_weight * min(age, config.max_aging_seconds)
+        c.score -= tenant_penalty(c.tenant_id)
+    chosen = max(candidates, key=lambda c: c.score)
--- a/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/queueing.py
+++ b/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/queueing.py
@@ -30,6 +30,28 @@ class TenantBucket:
+    def allow(self, tenant_id, tokens=1):
+        # simple token bucket per tenant to ensure fairness across tenants
+        bucket = self.buckets.setdefault(tenant_id, TokenBucket(self.rate, self.capacity))
+        return bucket.consume(tokens)
--- a/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/preempt.py
+++ b/src/runtime/continuous_batcher/preempt.py
@@ -1,6 +1,28 @@
+def should_preempt(running_batch, waiting_request):
+    wait_ms = (time.monotonic() - waiting_request.enqueue_time) * 1000
+    if wait_ms > config.preempt_threshold_ms and running_batch.estimated_remaining_ms > config.preempt_min_remaining_ms:
+        return True
+    return False
review_comments: Aisha: Can you explain the safety boundary for preemption? I want to ensure we don't introduce jitter for throughput-oriented workloads.
Samir: Nit: consider pulling aging_weight into the per-route config so enterprise customers can tune independently.
Priya: Tests look solid. I want an additional stress scenario with 200 tenants and very skewed qps to validate token bucket behavior.
author_responses: Oliver: Preemption is best-effort and only triggers when estimated_remaining > preempt_min_remaining_ms to avoid thrash. Added comments and a defensive metric to count preempt churn.
Oliver: Good call on per-route config - I added documentation and made aging_weight overridable at route-level in the config with sane defaults.
Oliver: Added the 200-tenant stress scenario to the bench harness; results appended to the test file and CI runs include the stressbench in a gated perf job.
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce p99 latency and prevent starvation for low-throughput routes. New config knobs: aging_weight, preempt_threshold_ms, fairness_tokens. New metrics added: batch_wait_seconds, request_age_p50/p95/p99, preempted_batches. Backwards compatible defaults; no breaking changes.
